messages.subject: WITHOUT PREJUDICE - Whitcombe v Sutherland Logistics
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Ms Bartlett,

Please find attached a without prejudice letter setting out our client's offer to resolve this matter. In short, our client offers £85,000 in full and final settlement, a £10,000 plus VAT contribution to your client's legal costs, an agreed reference and standard confidentiality.

The offer is open for 21 days. We are, of course, willing to discuss.

Kind regards,
Sarah Whitfield
Partner | Employment & Dispute Resolution
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 0521

Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: WITHOUT PREJUDICE - Whitcombe v Sutherland Logistics
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Ms Whitfield,

Thank you for your letter. Our client has considered it carefully but regards £85,000 as falling well short of the value of a claim where the compensatory cap does not apply. Our client's position is that a figure of £125,000, together with a £17,500 costs contribution and payment within 14 days, would resolve matters. He feels strongly about the maintenance issue and is prepared to give evidence about it.

We remain hopeful that the gap can be bridged.

Yours sincerely,
Eleanor Bartlett
Partner
Ashworth Quinn LLP
8 Temple Row, Birmingham B2 5HG
DDI 0121 246 7702

messages.subject: RE: WITHOUT PREJUDICE - Whitcombe v Sutherland Logistics
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Ms Bartlett,

Thank you. Our client is not able to meet £125,000, which in our view does not reflect the litigation risk on your client's side - in particular the strength of the redundancy rationale and the issues with mitigation. By way of a genuine attempt to close this out, our client will increase its offer to £108,000 in full and final settlement, a £15,000 (incl. VAT) costs contribution, payment within 21 days, and the agreed reference already proposed. This is at the top of our client's authority and is not a staging post to a higher number.

If your client accepts in principle we will circulate a settlement agreement for the statutory advice to be given.

Kind regards,
Sarah Whitfield
Partner | Employment & Dispute Resolution
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 0521

Confidential and may be legally privileged.
